note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a venue has, what a session costs, whether it is lit - come from the City of Tallahassee and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Leon County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the third county in Florida this directory has published in, after Lee and Hillsborough, and one city of it is on this page.

slots.coverage: One city in Leon County is published here: Tallahassee, with seven venues and thirty-four courts verified against the City's own pickleball page, thirty-three of them outdoors and one inside Jake Gaither Community Center. Nothing else in the county has been read. Leon County's own parks have not been checked against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site and this page does not characterise them - not their court counts, not whether they publish any. What this page reports is what the City of Tallahassee writes down: a count and an address for every venue, a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and first-come hours for the outdoor courts, a price table for Reserved Play, a free answer for Open Play, hours at one venue, lighting at one, and surface nowhere. Five venues inside Tallahassee itself are absent and named on the city page rather than dropped. Four Oaks Park has six courts "used for pickleball only" and a schedule seven days a week, at an address neither address resolver can find. Four community centres - Lawrence-Gregory, Lincoln, Sue Herndon McCollum and the Tallahassee Senior Center - are on the City's indoor schedule with sessions and no court count, and Lincoln reads "renovations in progress" on every day. Each is one fact away from being here: an address that resolves, or a number the City has not written.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county is concentrated in one city and, within it, split between parks and community centres in a way the City's own list makes plain. Three of the seven venues are parks - Tom Brown with twelve courts, Winthrop with six, Lafayette with two - and four are community centres with courts outside the building: LeVerne Payne with six, Walker-Ford with three, Jake Gaither with two outdoors and one in, McLean with two. Eighteen of the thirty-four courts are at the two parks the City takes online reservations for, Tom Brown and Winthrop, and fourteen of those eighteen are tennis courts doing double duty - eight of Tom Brown's on "tennis courts 1-4" and all six of Winthrop's "multi-purpose courts". The useful pattern is the schedule rather than the map. Two venues carry free Open Play sessions, LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, and they are the two where a rotation is guaranteed by the City's timetable; two carry paid Reserved Play, Tom Brown and Winthrop; four are first come, first play at every hour with no session at all. Lighting is stated once, at Walker-Ford, three courts. Hours are stated once, at Jake Gaither. The one indoor court in the county's published set is Jake Gaither's, on a Friday lunchtime, Reserved Play only. Nothing here is a complex, and that is a fact about what publishes rather than about what the City has built: the complex is Four Oaks Park, absent for want of an address that resolves.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a Tallahassee page wearing the heading of a county, and the gap will not close by accident. Leon County's own parks have not been read; no other operator in the county has been read; the threshold has not moved - three venues with a named source and a date - and nothing on this page says whether anything outside the City would clear it. Inside Tallahassee the gaps are of two kinds. The first is the five refused venues, which are real places on the City's own list. Four Oaks is the expensive one: six dedicated courts, Open Play and Reserved Play seven days a week to 10:00pm, online booking, and an address, "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", that returns nothing from the Census address file and nothing at house-number level from OpenStreetMap. The four indoor centres fail on a number the City has not written, and the City's indoor list is otherwise detailed enough - sessions, phone numbers, a "$3 Donation Encouraged" at the Senior Center - that the missing count is conspicuous. The second kind is silence inside published venues: no surface anywhere, lighting at one venue in seven, hours at one, and a resurfacing notice at McLean dated December 2025 that was still on the page in September 2026. Nothing outside a municipal parks department appears here at all, and that absence is about who writes things down rather than where the game is played.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Leon County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 34 courts across seven venues, all in Tallahassee, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Tallahassee alone names five further venues we cannot publish, one of them with six pickleball-only courts, and no other operator in the county has been read.

Because it is the only operator in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Leon County's own parks have not been read, and nothing on this page says what they would show if they were.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Two venues are, during Open Play: LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, where the City writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Reserved Play at Tom Brown and Winthrop costs $3.50 to $5.75 a session. The other four venues are first come, first play with no stated price, so they carry no fee answer.

One, on the City's phrase rather than the word: Walker-Ford Community Center, "3 courts - night play is available". No other venue in the county's published set carries a lighting statement, so the rest are recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit.

faqs.q: What is Four Oaks Park, and why is it not listed?
faqs.a: The City's flagship: six courts "used for pickleball only", Open Play and Reserved Play seven days a week to 10:00pm, and online booking through Court Reserve. The City prints its address as "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", and neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find it, so it fails the one gate that needs a street address that resolves.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and every one of them is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If the City changes a count, removes the resurfacing notice at McLean, or prints an address for Four Oaks that resolves, the build fails and someone reads the page again.

sources.evidence: The seven published addresses matched at house-number level and were placed in Leon County, FL (FIPS 12073), inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city - five through the Census address file as the City writes them, and two (Tom Brown Park as "501 EASTERWOOD DR", Lafayette Park as "501 INGLESIDE AVE") on Census answers that change the City's street type where OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the City's spelling. "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", the address the City publishes for Four Oaks Park, is found by neither resolver. Snapshot: data/sources/tallahassee-county-census.json
